# A classic example

Let's get things set up:
```{python setup}
import pandas as pd
import plotnine as p9

```
and use the [Palmer Penguins](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/articles/intro.html)
dataset

```{python data}
from plotnine.data import penguins
```

## the data

```{python thedata}
penguins
```

## the data, v2

```{python thedata2}
pd.crosstab(penguins.species,  penguins.island)
```

## Let's make some plots!

```{python plot1}
(
    p9.ggplot(penguins,
        p9.aes(x='flipper_length_mm', y='body_mass_g', color='species')
    ) + p9.geom_point()
)
```

## What's going on there?

[plotnine](https://plotnine.org/guide/introduction.html)
is basically a port of [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/)
for python.

Have a look at the [cheatsheet](https://github.com/rstudio/cheatsheets/blob/main/plotnine.pdf):
```
ggplot(
    data,
    aes(...)
) + geom_function()
```
or, with all the bells and whistles:
```
ggplot(data=data_frame)
+ geom_function(
  mapping=aes(**mappings)
  stat=stat,
  position=position,
) + coord_function()
+ facet_function()
+ scale_function()
+ theme_function()
+ theme(**settings)
```
